card.name: Kancet Papatai
card.tagline: Kenyah Dayak war dance of a hero earning the Ajai title
card.profile: Kancet Papatai is a traditional war dance of the Dayak Kenyah people of East Kalimantan (Wikipedia). It depicts the story of a hero's battle against his enemies, highlighting his courage and the ceremony in which he is awarded the title 'Ajai' for victory. Performed by male dancers with agile, energetic and acrobatic movements punctuated by warrior cries, dancers wear the black beaded 'sapei sapaq' costume and carry the Mandau (the characteristic Kenyah sword) and the kelembit/kelambit wooden shield. The dance is accompanied by 'Sak Paku' songs and the sampe/sapeh, the traditional Dayak plucked lute.
card.insight: Often staged at Desa Budaya Pampang near Samarinda, Kancet Papatai preserves the martial ethos of the Kenyah's historic warrior and headhunting culture for contemporary cultural audiences (RRI.co.id).
card.image_significance: Dayak Kenyah hero war dance. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — E. Kalimantan (Kenyah), Indonesia.
